title: Universal halting with polynomial advice
statement: For every machine representation scheme $c$, the unary language consisting of numbers whose binary expansions begin with $1s$, where the suffix $s$ encodes a pair of an advice string and an input on which the machine decoded from that advice halts, belongs to polynomial-time with polynomial-length advice. Thus there are fixed polynomial bounds, an advice function of the specified polynomial length, and a finite binary Turing machine that decides this language within the specified time bound using that advice.
